title: 2008 HMMT February Combinatorics Problem 5
statement: Let \(S\) be the smallest subset of the integers with the property that \(0 \in S\) and for any \(x \in S\), we have \(3 x \in S\) and \(3 x+1 \in S\). Determine the number of non-negative integers in \(S\) less than 2008.

solutions.text: 128 Write the elements of \(S\) in their ternary expansion (i.e. base 3). Then the second condition translates into, if \(\overline{d_{1} d_{2} \cdots d_{k}} \in S\), then \(\overline{d_{1} d_{2} \cdots d_{k} 0}\) and \(\overline{d_{1} d_{2} \cdots d_{k} 1}\) are also in \(S\). It follows that \(S\) is the set of nonnegative integers whose tertiary representation contains only the digits 0 and 1. Since \(2 \cdot 3^{6}<2008<3^{7}\), there are \(2^{7}=128\) such elements less than 2008 . Therefore, there are 128 such non-negative elements.
